chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when it was the last ten days, would perform i'tikaf in the mosque, and a tent of hair would be pitched for him, and he would roll up his garment and fold his bed.
Some said, 'And he abstained from the women,' so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'As for abstaining from the women, no.'
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad abstain from his wives during i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific nature of the Prophet’s i'tikaf during the last ten days of Ramadan, distinguishing his spiritual seclusion from complete physical isolation from his wives. It highlights the scholarly distinction between 'i'tikaf' as a state of devotion within the mosque and the juristic ruling on marital relations, which remain permissible unless explicitly vowed otherwise. This context is crucial for understanding the flexibility of Sunnah practices in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions of spiritual retreat.
